result.summary: One code design for REQ-116 and REQ-117 (task M2.3) in docs/design/M2PROJ-invites-projects.md. It settles O11 of decisions/0137: a tenant route that writes has a plan (http/plan.js, a function stored beside the row like withBody, so a row keeps its four keys); the pipeline runs it on the platform part of the one request transaction before switchToTenant, appends the audit row it returns (organisation, actor and address from the session and the request, never from the plan), then switches and runs the handler under row-level security: one transaction, one connection, no way back from tenant to platform (measured: the audit row, the project and the version commit together and roll back together). It specifies migration 0003_projects.sql (projects and idea_versions with composite organisation keys, forced RLS and an insert-only trigger whose one exception is the purge setting app.purge_org; user_consents; deletion_requests; invites.owner_identity and org_name with a check; widened audit action and re-auth purpose checks; a users guard trigger), the grants.sql blocks, the 0003 rehearsal seed, 14 new routes (N1-N14: 2 public invite, 1 account, 7 admin, 4 tenant) with metadata, request, answer, error codes and the roles on each route, 8 new error codes (AUTH_CODES 31), the invite flow (128-bit code, HMAC, 7 days, one conditional UPDATE claim after every check and the password hash, returned vs thrown refusals, the G7 constant owner_only, registration modes, the e-mail binding, the consent digest of the exact sentence shown), the five consent sentences with the kk draft and the narrow word-list exception (CONSENT_KEYS, DELETION_TERM, stripDeletionTerm), the deletion request and the admin deletion (placeholders, removals, scrub of the used invite's e-mail, the purge helper for an organisation left without members), project creation with three quick facts and the 20 per day limit, versioned ideas with a reason (version number under the project row lock), the stage module (11 stages, 20 allowed pairs), the board, the card (one admin_read row per call), the audit page, the KZ formats module, the footer of every M2 page, ten pages with an element-id contract, and the e2e path. issues.text: decisions/0137 O11 (how the audit row of a tenant action commits with the action) is settled in the design as C1 and 4.4: the plan hook, run on the platform part of the request transaction before switchToTenant; measured in F5. Proposal for a decisions record: decisions/0138-m2proj-code-design-conventions.md with the section «Основание», holding C1-C20 and the answers to O1-O10.

REQ-117 criteria 3 and 9 print `update projects` and `delete from idea_versions` as lines of app/server/services/projects.js only, while DBC-1 of REQ-115 (released, db-calls.test.js) forbids any database call outside app/server/db/ and M2AUTH 4.5.4 puts every statement in a store (F16). Recommended: the statements stand in app/server/db/project-store.js and REQ-117 criteria 3 and 9 are micro-amended by REQ-ANALYST and REQ-VALIDATOR (the greps name project-store.js; the meaning is unchanged) before step 2. The design's tests STG-4 and DEL-8 name the file of this answer.

Re-auth purposes. (a) POST /api/admin/invites consumes the purpose owner_identity on every invite (meta.reauth cannot depend on the body; REQ-116 asks the token for an owner identity only, but under G7 owner_only every invite is for one). (b) POST /api/admin/users/:id/delete needs a token and the REQ names no purpose: a new purpose user_delete (the closed table of M2AUTH 4.9.4, the 0003 check, two test literals, ARCH §5). Recommended: yes to both.

REQ-116 names no source for the name of a new customer organisation, and IS-4 refuses a body key org_id or orgId on every route (F17). Recommended: the owner types the name on the invite (org_name, 1-120, a column of invites with a check against organisation); an existing organisation is named by the body key `organisation`; the invited person never names an organisation (so no personal name lands in orgs.name, which stays after a deletion).

REQ-117 asks for «the allowed transitions» without a table. Recommended: the minimal forward table of design 4.7 (20 of the 121 pairs: draft->interview->spec->approved->dev_requested->in_development->built->delivered, delivered->accepted, delivered->returned, returned->in_development, and archived from every other stage); M3-M5 extend it by a «was -> became» row. A decisions record.

Consent language: the server accepts a consent only in a language whose five sentences its served texts hold (the open build drops kk values, F14), so on production ru and en; the kk draft (FOR_NATIVE_SPEAKER) is refused with consent_stale and not listed by GET /api/invites/:code. Recommended: yes.

ARCH §14.5 lists «admin read of tenant data»; REQ-117 criterion 5 audits the card only. Recommended: audit the card (one admin_read row per call), not the board list (titles, organisation names, times).

Personal data in invites (the invited e-mail): (a) the lazy cleanup removes unused invites expired more than 30 days ago (ARCH §4 retention; invites gets the DELETE grant); (b) the deletion replaces the e-mail of the invites that user used by the placeholder. Recommended: yes to both (decisions/0100 items 1 and 5).
A deletion request by the platform admin is refused with 403 forbidden (his account cannot be deleted; a request that can never be carried out is not stored). Recommended: yes.

decisions/0137 O6 says G21 comes with the client-facing pages of REQ-116 and REQ-117, but the route of this run has no GUI-DESIGN-ANALYST step (WF-04) before step 2. The design builds functional pages on the existing styles with a closed element-id contract. ORCH decides: insert a WF-04 look description of the invite, project list, new project and project pages before step 2, or build as designed and ask G21 on the UAT screens (a look change then reworks sub-step F4 only).

A client-side idea edit form on project.html: the route POST /api/projects/:id/idea is required by criterion 2, the form is not. Recommended: include the small form for members and above (the client's only way to correct his own idea on the goal path); a viewer sees none.

Facts of the task checked: the base tag is 60b10b7 and app/.github equal main 6078bfb (F1); the route table has 15 rows, AUTH_CODES 23, PURPOSES 11 (F2). The REQ-116 criteria's `grep -rnwl is_owner_identity` is met by the design's list of two files (db/auth-store.js, db/org-store.js): the column of invites is named owner_identity so the whole-word grep does not match it.

Not measurable on this PC (no Postgres): the row lock of the version number and of the invite claim under real concurrency; the design names M2R-1, M2R-2 and M2R-3 (pg job) as their proof. PGlite serialises transactions, so the int tests INV-6 and the PGlite run of the version race prove the logic only (F11).

Proposed anti-patterns for DOC-UPDATER (Q13): a hook that appends an audit row after the switch to tenant settings is refused by the writer; a guard suite that sends an empty body to every object route hides a 404 behind a 400; a legitimate body key named org_id turns the key-refusal suite red; an exact-path list of routes that change the session misses a route with a path parameter.
